fields.subject: MEDI
fields.question_text: A 45-year-old presents with paroxysmal palpitations. ECG shows a narrow-complex tachycardia at 180/min, regular, with no discernible P waves. Vagal manoeuvres terminate the arrhythmia. The most likely mechanism is:
fields.option_a: Increased automaticity in the SA node
fields.explanation: AVNRT — AV nodal re-entrant tachycardia — is the commonest paroxysmal SVT, terminated by vagal tone (which slows AV node conduction enough to break the re-entry loop).
fields.concept_explanation: AVNRT involves dual AV-nodal pathways (fast + slow). A premature beat blocks the fast pathway, conducts down the slow pathway, then re-enters retrogradely up the fast pathway → circus movement within the AV node.
fields.mnemonic: AVNRT = AV Node Re-entry Tachycardia; Valsalva terminates because vagal tone slows the slow pathway.

fields.subject: OPHI
fields.question_text:
The fundus photograph shown belongs to a 62-year-old with gradually decreasing peripheral vision.
[[img:glaucomatous_cup_91.png]]
Which finding on the disc supports a diagnosis of primary open-angle glaucoma?
fields.option_a: Increased cup-to-disc ratio with notching of the neuroretinal rim
fields.explanation: Glaucomatous optic neuropathy: increased cup-to-disc ratio (>0.6), focal notching of the neuroretinal rim, bayoneting of vessels, disc haemorrhages, RNFL defects on perimetry.
fields.concept_explanation: POAG is an asymmetric, slowly progressive optic neuropathy with characteristic cup enlargement. Unlike angle-closure glaucoma, the angle is open on gonioscopy.

fields.subject: PTHI
fields.question_text: A 5-year-old child presents with pallor and splenomegaly. Peripheral smear shows target cells and nucleated red blood cells. HPLC shows HbF = 90%, HbA2 = 3%, HbA absent. The condition is:
fields.explanation:
β-thalassemia major: β-globin chains are absent → HbA (β2γ2 = α2β2) is absent; γ-chains rise compensatorily → HbF (α2γ2) dominates.

Reference diagram [[img:globin_chain_synthesis.png]]: comparison of β-thal major vs trait vs silent carrier on HPLC.
fields.concept_explanation: Defect lies in HBB gene on chromosome 11. In β-thal major, both β-globin alleles are affected (β0/β0 or β+/β+ severe). Marrow expansion gives 'crew-cut' skull X-ray; iron overload from repeated transfusions causes secondary haemochromatosis.
fields.mnemonic: β-thal major = Marrow Markedly Expands = 'Crew cut' skull.
